clue.text: Rule cat out when worried about large decapitated rodent in drawer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, or around, the next piece
worried letters are fretted and pulled about, so the words rule cat out are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: a decapitated word loses its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A nervous cat lover is asked to let the cat out while a half-eaten rodent lies in a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges RULE CAT OUT into TOU...LAUTREC, which goes 'about' L plus OUSE ('decapitated' removes the M from MOUSE). 'drawer' is someone who draws, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The French artist was a prolific draughtsman and poster designer, so he is a drawer in the sense of one who draws.

clue.text: Like what can be cured, cooked in ale batter?

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared and altered, so the letters of ale batter are reworked

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chips cook wonders if beer batter might be a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' hints at meat preserved by salting, sitting with the cooking theme, but here it means healed.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness that responds to medical care, that a doctor can deal with, is curable.

clue.text: Pawnbroker fleeced many? That's morally wrong

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

indicators.note: a fleeced sheep loses its outer coat, so the outer letters of many are stripped away

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker cheated lots of people, which is immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeced' looks like 'swindled', fitting a pawnbroker, but it shears the ends off MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean in a religious or moral sense means impure or sinful.

clue.text: Make the best use of one tip some produced

indicators.note: produced means brought out in a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to make the most of a single tip that some people came up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the most out of something, or arrange it for peak effect, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Holy man in blue hotel uniform

parts.note: blue means sad, low
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A holy man is seen in a blue hotel uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic, a wandering holy man who has renounced worldly life.

clue.text: Gallery at home? Finally, one invites His Majesty

parts.note: a loft can be an upper gallery, as an organ loft in a church
in means at home

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone in a gallery at home finally invites the King in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His Majesty' reads as one royal title, but 'His' gives a last letter and 'Majesty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is stately grandeur or nobility, a lofty, exalted quality.

clue.text: Sort of sunflower? That's doubtful

indicators.note: sort of suggests a variant, so the letters of sun are reworked

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Is this a kind of sunflower? Someone isn't sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Ure in north Yorkshire, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being doubtful about something is being uncertain, not confident of it.

clue.text: Literary circle de rigueur on Dürer's part

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the letters of these words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Discussing a circle of writers, it seems essential on the painter Dürer's part.
explanation.walkthrough: The umlaut is ignored. 'Literary circle' looks like a book club, but it means a round shape in literary language.
explanation.definitionFit: Rondure is a poetic word for a circle or roundness, used chiefly in literature.

clue.text: Someone appealing from courtside regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of courtside, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tennis player appeals to the umpire from courtside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appealing' looks like making a line-call appeal, but it means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, charming person, one who is appealing to look at.

clue.text: Former lover reportedly seen beside yourself

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for seen is heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: seen means sighted

explanation.surface: Someone notices their former partner has been spotted sitting next to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns SIGHTED (seen) into its sound-alike CITED. 'beside yourself' looks like a position next to you but is the idiom for being overwrought.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beside yourself is an idiom for being agitated, worked up or thrilled beyond self-control.

clue.text: Rock off Ireland, nippy place for catching fish

parts.note: nippy means quick
fish are caught in a net

explanation.surface: A rocky spot off the Irish coast is described as a quick place to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fastnet is a rocky islet off County Cork in southern Ireland, famous for its lighthouse and the yacht race named after it.

clue.text: Using some paint, he bedaubed 23 down

indicators.note: only some of the letters of paint he bedaubed are used, a run lying inside those words

explanation.surface: A painter is said to have daubed some paint on one of the picture's subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference to 23 down, the French title of the same Toulouse-Lautrec painting, of which this is the English translation.
explanation.definitionFit: The 23 down entry is the French title of a Toulouse-Lautrec painting of two women in a bed; this is its English rendering.

clue.text: Short time for all to see brief relationship with 1 across's red can repeated here

parts.note: mo is a short form of moment, a brief time
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for universal viewing

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a link is a connection or relationship
the artist was French, and rouge is French for red

explanation.surface: A quick, open fling is set in the painter's world with red paint and a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can repeated' gives can-can, the dance famously performed at this Paris cabaret, which Toulouse-Lautrec painted and drew posters for.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cabaret is the classic home of the cancan dance, a can doubled up into the dance's name.

clue.text: Provider of treatment after a break? One based in British 22, perhaps

definitions.text: Provider of treatment after a break

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the first pair of words go inside the outer letters

parts.note: 22 down is street, and a terrace, abbreviated Ter, is one kind of street
a story based in Paris is set in Paris, so based means set

explanation.surface: Someone is described as living in a typical British road and offering treatment after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a break' suggests a holiday, but the break is a fractured bone. Ter is the postal abbreviation for Terrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional practitioner who resets dislocated or fractured bones provides treatment once a limb is broken.

clue.text: Setting for one of setter's anagrams

definitions.text: Setting for one of setter's anagrams

parts.words: Setting for one of setter's anagrams
parts.note: an anagram of the word setter is a road, and that word is the answer at 22 down, so this number is where it is set in the grid

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter is asked where they place one of their anagrams.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 down answer rearranges the letters of 'setter', so the number 22 is the setting for one of setter's anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid number of the clue whose answer is an anagram of setter locates that word, so the number is its place.

clue.text: Personification of youth portrayed in 11 25

indicators.note: portrayed in means the letters appear inside the linked entry, so its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: 11 25 is the linked entry, the English name of the painting

explanation.surface: A painting of a young goddess is said to appear in the artist's bed picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside the answer to the linked 11 and 25 across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this daughter of Zeus and Hera was the goddess and embodiment of youth, cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: One who hastens through loosely roped exit

indicators.note: loosely suggests letters set free from their order, so roped exit is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rushes out through an exit marked off loosely with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: An expeditor speeds things along, someone who hurries a process up to completion.

clue.text: Flower girl has gone travelling around Spain in the main

parts.note: Iris is both a flower and a girl's name

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters round the next piece
gone travelling means the letters have wandered from their places, so has is rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A girl called after a flower has gone off travelling around Spain by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old word for the open sea. 'gone travelling' turns HAS into HSA, which goes 'around' E.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the sea, and this stretch of water lies between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Writer injecting heroin, next but one after Charlie

indicators.note: injecting puts one piece inside another, here the drug inside the writer's name

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A writer is shooting up heroin, right after someone called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a person or cocaine, keeping the drug theme, but it is the NATO phonetic letter C; D is Delta, and the one after that is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, Charlie is C, Delta D, and the code word for E follows those two.

clue.text: Ring for answer in German port? On your head be it!

indicators.note: Ring for answer means the letter for ring replaces the letter for answer

parts.note: Hamburg is a major port in northern Germany
a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A ring is ordered in a German port, with a warning that the consequences are yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your head be it!' is the idiom for taking responsibility, but here it is literal: it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a felt hat with a dented crown, worn on the head, so the idiom becomes literal.

clue.text: Use of blue pencil in Paris, chosen after moving out of Albi originally

indicators.note: after moving signals the letters are rearranged, once the named letter has moved out of them
originally means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A editor in Paris was picked after leaving the southern town of Albi.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A ('Albi originally') from PARIS CHOSEN and rearrange ('moving') the rest. A blue pencil is the editor's or censor's tool for striking out material.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking out material with a blue pencil is the classic image of an official cutting objectionable content.

clue.text: Explosive black artist taking the first chorus at beginning of Israelites

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

indicators.note: at beginning means the first letter of chorus is taken

explanation.surface: A volatile black artist takes the lead in a chorus at the start of an Israelite song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at beginning of Israelites' looks like a first-letter pick from Israelites, but 'at beginning' takes C from chorus and 'of Israelites' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the Hebrews, the ancient people of Israel, or their language.

clue.text: One of 1 across's subjects walks in this way

definitions.text: One of 1 across's subjects walks in this way

parts.words: One of 1 across's subjects walks in this way
parts.note: the painter often depicted prostitutes, women said to ply their trade by walking the pavements, so this word goes before walker

explanation.surface: One of the painter's models walks a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus 'walker' names a prostitute, one of Toulouse-Lautrec's frequent subjects; she walks in this public way.
explanation.definitionFit: A prostitute soliciting outdoors works the public road, so she walks along this way, a road.

clue.text: Checks 50 copies

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
imitations are copies

explanation.surface: Someone checks fifty forgeries.
explanation.definitionFit: Checks as a noun are restraints or restrictions, things that hold something back.

clue.text: 1 across's portrayal of musical elitism

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the words musical elitism

explanation.surface: The painter is said to depict snobbery about music.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the French title of a Toulouse-Lautrec painting of two women lying in bed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-titled painting by Toulouse-Lautrec shows two women in bed, one of the artist's works.

clue.text: Comedian that is funny at first

indicators.note: at first means the word for funny is placed first, before the abbreviation

parts.note: funny means odd, strange
ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a comedian was funny to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Oddie is a British comedian of The Goodies, later a TV birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Oddie is a British comic performer, best known as one of The Goodies.

clue.text: See 11
Place of pilgrimage: not right spot, ultimately, to be extremely flashy

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: Lourdes in southern France is a Catholic pilgrimage site

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A pilgrim site is judged the wrong place to be showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely flashy' is the definition: most flashy, as a loud shirt is garish.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud describes garish, showy colours or clothes, so the superlative means most flashy of all.

clue.text: High line from tenor accompanying exotic dances

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters of dances are rearranged

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for tenor in choral scoring

explanation.surface: A tenor sings a high part to go with some foreign dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'accompanying' only join; T goes after the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung or played above the main tune, typically by trebles in a hymn.

clue.text: 1 across's portrayal of contents of red can knocked over by drunk guy?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a guy is a rope used to hold a tent steady

indicators.note: the contents of the words red can are their letters, to be reworked
knocked over suggests spilt and jumbled, so the letters of red can are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk man knocks over a can of red paint in the artist's studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' and 'knocked over' together rearrange RED CAN. Toulouse-Lautrec drew circus performers, including a woman on a high wire.
explanation.definitionFit: The artist drew and painted circus acts, and a high-wire performer is one of those subjects.
